dsd_direct: Does the DSD stream reach the conversion stage without passing through an internal filter? This field decides ONE thing and one only: whether a per-device correction could ever apply, i.e. correctable. It does NOT decide whether Auto sends DSD - that is dsd_reconverted_to_pcm, and conflating the two is the mistake this catalogue made until 2026-11-20. Values: true, false, firmware_dependent, to_be_measured. Beware of vocabulary: some manufacturers confuse "DSD Direct" with "Native DSD". The latter only describes the transport. Only measurement settles it.
dsd_reconverted_to_pcm: Does the device bring DSD back to PCM internally before converting? Decisive, and the only field that makes Auto send PCM to a DSD-capable device: a converter that re-converts has nothing to gain from receiving DSD, because it would redo - worse - the work we have just done. true, false, or null when no evidence settles it. null is permissive: with no evidence of re-conversion, Auto sends DSD. Requires evidence in source, exactly like dsd_direct, and is never inferred from it: a device can fail to be bit-exact (dsd_direct false) and still convert the DSD it is given, which is the ESS case.
analog_filter: Quality of the analog reconstruction stage: switchable, good, simple, weak. Feeds the modulator order decision - order 5 suits simple stages, order 7 demands a good filter.
correctable: Whether a per-device correction profile could ever apply. Precondition stated by the author: a DAC too far from bit-perfect performs varying internal DSP that does not let the correction reach the conversion stage consistently. In practice corrections exist only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM. See _device_correction.
device_settings: Settings to make on the device itself, not in the module.
usb: USB identity, the key automatic identification matches on. vid and pid are the USB vendor and product identifiers as integers; product_strings are the manufacturer and product strings the device declares, lowercased and stripped. NEVER guess these: an identity filled from memory makes the engine assert a technology, a modulator order and a level offset for the wrong device, and a wrong record is worse than no record. Fill them from the device itself, or from the Linux kernel USB audio quirk tables. A record with a null vid is still usable by name — it simply never matches automatically.
_what_the_chip_fixes: Three fields, and only three, are properties of the silicon and are therefore safe to inherit from the family without ever checking the device: modulator_order, pcm_dsd_level_offset_db, and shaper_linearization. They do not vary between two devices built on the same chip, and a record that restates them is restating the family.
_what_the_implementation_fixes: Everything else belongs to the device, not to the chip: pcm_max_hz, dsd_max, native_dsd, dop, analog_filter. These are decided by the USB receiver, the firmware and the output stage. The four ESS records in this file make the point - 384 kHz on exaSound and Merging against 768 on Topping, DSD256 against DSD512, and a good analog stage on the NADAC where the others are simple. Same chip, four different sets of numbers.
_the_field_that_fools_people: Two fields here look like one, and until 2026-11-20 they were one. dsd_direct asks whether the stream reaches conversion unfiltered, which governs correctable. dsd_reconverted_to_pcm asks whether the device undoes our work, which governs whether Auto sends DSD at all. The Denafrips evidence establishes the second ("it doesn't do bit-perfect DSD conversion, but instead runs some kind of PCM conversion"); the ESS family note establishes only the first. Merging them silenced DSD on every ESS device and made the order-5 modulator rule unreachable - dead code found by reading the catalogue against itself. Neither field is a property of the chip, with the one exception below. The six AKM records here carry three different dsd_direct values. Never infer either from the chip: measure, or cite a documented answer about that device. This is why source is required on every record.
_the_ess_exception: ESS is the one family that fixes dsd_direct, at false, for every device: the chip leaves makers no choice, since everything passes through its internal DSP in PCM and DSD alike. Hence correctable = false across the family - a correction cannot travel through variable processing we do not control. It does NOT fix dsd_reconverted_to_pcm, which the family sets to false: the author recommends DSD output to ESS parts by name, and a fifth-order modulator before the ES9039. The exception is about correctability, and nothing else.
_where_the_family_is_too_coarse: ess_sabre does not distinguish an ES9018 from an ES9038PRO. The family's three assertions hold across the Sabre line with one soft spot: switching_elements = single, which is what yields a 5th order modulator. A device paralleling eight ES9038PRO channels is arguably multi-element, hence 7th order. The catalogue follows the source, which states the rule at brand level. If such a device turns up, this is exactly what a device record is for: a record overrides its family field by field, and the override needs its own evidence.
brand: The maker, as a key into brands.json. "unknown" where no brand is known, which is the state of the two chip-family fallbacks. Separating the brand from the model is what keeps the listener's first list short and what lets a fact true of a whole range be written once.
model: The model alone, without the maker's name: "May", not "Holo Audio May". The value "unknown" marks the brand's CATCH-ALL record - what Auto resolves when the listener knows who made their converter but not which one, and what the model list's own "I don't know" entry selects. Five records here are catch-alls, and before the split they were hiding inside the name field as "Chord (Qutest, Hugo, Dave)" or "Denafrips (Ares / Pontus / Venus / Terminator)" - brand-level assertions wearing the shape of a device.
internal_bypass: Some converters stop processing the signal themselves once the incoming rate is high enough: feed them above a threshold and their own interpolation stage is out of the path. That is worth more than the rate itself, because it removes a stage we do not control and cannot correct for. Fields: format, at_or_above_hz, bypasses (what stops, in words), strength ("prefer" raises the candidate's score, "require" makes it a floor), and source. The engine reports it in the trace, so a listener fed 705.6 kHz on a converter that accepts 768 learns why. Not a quirk of one maker: the pattern recurs wherever a device has an internal filter it will step aside from.
_unknown: Every field in this catalogue has three possible states and they must stay distinguishable. A VALUE means known at this level. ABSENT means this level says nothing, so the level above decides - model, then brand, then chip family, then the global default. The string "unknown" means this level has looked and there is no answer: a finished state, not a blank, and the engine takes the conservative branch instead of substituting a default. null is gone from the catalogue and forbidden by the schema. It used to carry both "nobody filled this in" and "nobody knows", which are opposite facts about where to spend effort, and in one record it silently erased a chip family's bit depth. That is a better answer than the escape hatch written the morning after the defect was reported.
_entry_criterion: A model record is admissible when it meets BOTH of these, and no number of filled fields substitutes for either. ONE: every field it states has a source naming that device - the rule validate.py enforces, and the one the Gustard records failed for months while looking complete. TWO: it carries either a USB identity or at least one fact its brand does not already supply. A record that states nothing its brand has not already stated, and cannot be matched automatically, is a row that adds a name to a list and knowledge to nothing. See _completeness for what each further level buys and who has to do the work.
provenance: Which inlet a fact came through - probe, maker, listener or agent - as distinct from source, which is the citation itself. Two different questions: source says what was read, provenance says how much to trust it and who to go back to. Recorded per field group rather than per record, since one record routinely mixes a probe's ceilings with a forum answer about its internals. See _governance.
chip: What the conversion stage actually is, in words. A part number where there is one, a count where there are several, or the maker's own design named as such. It is DOCUMENTATION, not a dispatch key: the engine reads family and technology and never this. It exists so that a converter built by its maker can be described precisely without inventing a family that would carry no defaults - see chips.json _a_makers_own_converter.
technology: What the conversion stage is: delta_sigma, r2r, discrete_dsd or fpga. This is what the ENGINE dispatches on - it decides whether a shaper can linearise the stage - while family is a bundle of defaults. A record needs no family and can state every field itself; it resolves perfectly and the engine never notices. But a record without a family MUST state technology, because the fallback is delta_sigma: right for most converters, wrong for every resistor ladder and every discrete DSD stage, and until 2026-11-20 applied silently. validate.py now refuses the combination of no family and no technology.
